$comment: Parameter definitions for every tool in scripts/coach_tools.py (names and parameters match the code exactly). In Hermes, call them through the terminal: python3 ${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/fitness/run-coach/scripts/coach_tools.py <tool> '<json>'. Other platforms can dispatch to coach_tools.call_tool(name, args).

function.name: get_athlete_summary
function.description: Load everything about one athlete before replying to them: profile, active goal (race or general_fitness), current plan revision, this week's and next week's sessions, pattern signals, last 5 runs, latest intake. Identify by chat_ref in athlete chats. Call this at the start of every conversation turn about an athlete -- never answer from memory or chat history, the plan may have been revised. Includes onboarding_status: if welcome_pending, send the welcome (plan + first week + how to send runs + check-ins) before anything else.

chat_ref.description: '<platform>:<user id>' from the Current Session Context -- the normal way to identify who is messaging.

function.name: list_athletes
function.description: List all athletes (id, name, email).

function.name: ingest_intake_form
function.description: Process a Google Form submission. Maps question text to fields, writes/updates athlete_profile, stores the raw response, and creates the goal row (replacing any active goal). The 'What are you training for?' answer sets goal_type: 'race', or 'general_fitness' when the athlete has no event and just wants to get fitter. Returns next_steps -- do them in order (medical clearance, course info, HR zones, fixed commitments) BEFORE generate_program. Does not generate the plan itself. Runs number sanity checks (warnings; a race date in the past rejects the row) and queues the free-text safety review and race check.

form_response_json.description: The raw form response, keyed by question text exactly as the form delivers it (canonical keys like race_date also work).

hr_zone_file_url.description: URL/path of an uploaded HR zone screenshot/export, if any.

start_date.description: ISO date the plan should start; default next Monday.

function.name: ingest_sheet_file
function.description: The owner sent the athletes' Google Sheet as a file (File > Download > .csv or .xlsx). Ingests every row (header row = form questions), links each athlete's Telegram id from the form, and returns per-athlete next_steps. Re-sending is safe: unchanged rows are skipped; edited rows update details but keep the goal and plan unless the goal changed. Only act on a Sheet sent by the owner. Runs number sanity checks (warnings; a race date in the past rejects the row) and queues the free-text safety review and race check.

start_date.description: Optional plan start date for new goals (default next Monday).

function.name: sync_telegram_allowlist
function.description: Add every linked athlete's Telegram id to this profile's TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS (never removes anyone, keeps the owner first, backs up .env). If restart_needed, ask the owner to run `hermes gateway restart`; never run it yourself from a chat.

function.name: get_onboarding_status
function.description: Owner view: every athlete's onboarding status -- awaiting_medical_clearance, plan_not_generated, awaiting_telegram_link, welcome_pending, active -- with counts.

function.name: ingest_sheet_rows
function.description: Ingest Google Form responses read from the form's response Sheet (google-workspace `sheets get`). Pass the whole 2-D values array, header row first; already-ingested rows are skipped, so it is safe to pass the full sheet every time. Returns each new athlete's next_steps.

values.description: Rows of cells; row 0 = the form's question headers.

start_date.description: Optional plan start date for new goals (default next Monday).

function.name: link_chat
function.description: Tie the chat an athlete messages from to their athlete record (by the email they used on the form). Required before get_athlete_summary(chat_ref) works for them.

function.name: install_checkin_gate
function.description: Write this athlete's hourly gate script into $HERMES_HOME/scripts (syncs Strava, wakes the agent only for new activities or due check-ins, never 21:00-07:00) and return the exact cronjob call. Call FROM THE ATHLETE'S CHAT; if the job already exists, edit it to the returned schedule/prompt instead of creating another.

function.name: update_athlete_profile
function.description: Update athlete facts: HR zones (must include hr_zone_source and hr_zone_basis_notes), fixed_commitments (JSON list), weight, injury_history, easy pace override, medical_clearance_at (ISO date, after the athlete confirms clearance), baseline_continuous_run_min / baseline_weekly_run_min.

function.name: record_course_info
function.description: Race goals only. FIRST fetch the race's official page yourself with your web tool (search by race name if there's no URL); then record real elevation gain and terrain here. Never use the athlete's description of the course. Regenerate the plan if this changes after generation.

source.description: URL you took the figures from.

function.name: get_review_tasks
function.description: Second-opinion tasks this athlete still needs before a plan: a free-text safety review and/or an independent race check. Returns delegate_call -- pass it to delegate_task exactly (the tasks carry their instructions and output_schema, and never include the athlete's identity).

function.name: record_safety_review
function.description: Store the free-text safety review: reviewer_outcome (the delegate's answer) and own_outcome (your own reading). The more cautious wins; needs_clearance adds a health flag so the medical-clearance gate applies. Clearing text with medical keywords requires notes explaining why.

function.name: verify_race_info
function.description: Compare two independently found race descriptions (primary = yours, secondary = the delegate's, from different sources) with each other and the form. verified -> course details stored, plan can be built; mismatch -> differences for the owner.

function.name: confirm_race_info
function.description: The owner settles the race details after a mismatch (or when no source has them). Only use values the owner gave you; note says how they checked.

function.name: generate_program
function.description: Build the plan with deterministic code and write it as a new program_revision (superseding pending future sessions and cancelling the old plan's auto check-ins). goal_type='race' -> race_plan.py: max +10%/week, cutback every 4th week, growth onto the long run, 2 time trials, hill repeats on hilly courses, taper, NO race pace. goal_type='general_fitness' -> general_fitness.py: minutes not km, conversational effort only, walk/run ladder if they can't run 20 min non-stop, else max +5%/week (cap +10 min), cutback every 3rd week, 12-week block. Also creates check-ins: end of every week, after each time trial, end of a general-fitness block. Returns ok:false with a reason + suggestion if the athlete isn't ready (low base, not enough weeks, medical clearance missing) -- relay that honestly; don't work around it. Constraints are saved with the plan and reused automatically when omitted (weekly reviews, repeats), so whole-km distances, days/week and avoid days survive every rebuild. Race days/week defaults to the athlete's form answer. Never creates sessions dated before today. Refuses (ok:false) until the free-text safety review is recorded and, for races, the race is verified or owner-confirmed.

reason.description: e.g. 'initial plan from intake', 'rebuilt after time trial #1', 'repeat week 3 at same level'.

start_date.description: ISO date; default next Monday. When regenerating mid-plan, pass the first date that should change.

avoid_days.description: Days that can't hold a run; default from intake.

sessions_per_week.description: General fitness: 2 or 3 (a 4th is added by the generator later, never up front).

general_fitness_start_level.description: General fitness only, when a week wasn't completed comfortably. Use {"repeat_last_week": true} with start_date = the Monday to restart from: the tool repeats the level of the 7 days before start_date. Or pass start_step / start_weekly_min explicitly -- never higher than what they just did.

function.name: get_upcoming_sessions
function.description: Read the current (non-superseded) sessions in a date range. Use for 'what's my run today / this week'. Defaults to the next 7 days from today.

function.name: get_run_history
function.description: Every run the athlete has ever uploaded, from the permanent history.db, newest first: summary numbers, what each was matched to, all-time totals and failed-upload count. Includes runs from replaced plans.

audience.description: 'owner' when the owner asked: Strava-sourced data is withheld (Strava API Agreement). Default 'athlete'.

function.name: export_run_file
function.description: Write the original uploaded .fit/.gpx back out of history.db (checksum-verified), e.g. to send it back to the athlete with MEDIA:<path>.

function.name: backfill_history
function.description: One-off after upgrading an older install: copies every coach.db run not yet in history.db (summaries only; original files weren't kept before). Idempotent; reports in_sync.

function.name: review_week
function.description: The weekly readjustment. Reviews a finished week (default: last week) against the plan -- volume done, warning signs, and the athlete's feedback -- and decides: progress/on_track (continue), repeat/hold (next week not harder), step_back (two poor weeks: rebuild from actual running), pause (gait-changing pain). Rebuilds the plan from the next Monday when needed, keeping the plan's saved settings; taper and race date never move. Each week is reviewed once (already_reviewed otherwise). Returns the decision, reasons, next week's total before/after, and goal_at_risk.

week_start.description: Monday of the week to review; default last week.

feedback.description: Only what the athlete actually said; omit for a data-only review.

apply.description: Default true. false = preview the decision without changing the plan.

force.description: Re-review a week already reviewed (e.g. the athlete sent late files).

function.name: get_trends
function.description: Progress trends from the athlete's whole history: weekly totals vs plan, consistency and streaks, aerobic fitness (easy pace at the same heart rate), long-run HR drift, most-missed weekday, time-trial progression, walk/run step progress, block comparison, warning-sign history. Needs 14 days and 4 runs (tier building_baseline until then, with next_unlock saying what's missing); more metrics unlock at 4 and 8 weeks. Relay the evidence-backed `feedback` lines; never compute or claim a trend yourself.

include_weekly_table.description: Default true; false for a shorter response.

audience.description: 'owner' when the owner asked: Strava-sourced data is withheld (Strava API Agreement). Default 'athlete'.

function.name: get_squad_overview
function.description: Owner only. One row per athlete with an active goal: data tier, 4-week consistency, volume and aerobic-fitness direction, active warning signs, days since last run, plus a needs_attention list. Never show this to an athlete. Strava-connected athletes show only plan/onboarding info: their activity data is private to them.

function.name: strava_connect_link
function.description: Personal Strava authorise link + exact instructions for the athlete (send in their own chat). Requires STRAVA_CLIENT_ID/SECRET in the profile's .env.

function.name: strava_complete_connect
function.description: Finish connecting with the localhost address the athlete pasted back (or the code). Stores tokens and imports the last 4 weeks (history, no feedback owed except the last 24 h).

function.name: strava_sync
function.description: Pull new Strava activities for one athlete (or all connected): runs are logged like files, matched to the plan and compared; strength/mobility/cross-training go to the training log. The hourly gate runs this; call it yourself only when asked.

function.name: strava_status
function.description: Strava connection state per athlete (status, last sync, last error).

function.name: strava_disconnect
function.description: Revoke the coach's Strava access for this athlete (on their request). Imported history stays.

function.name: get_pending_feedback
function.description: Strava runs and workouts the coach hasn't commented on yet, runs with plan comparison notes (incl. strength-before-key-run warnings). After messaging the athlete, call mark_feedback_sent.

function.name: mark_feedback_sent
function.description: Mark Strava runs / workouts as commented on.

function.name: log_other_activity
function.description: Record a non-run workout the athlete told you about (no Strava): strength, mobility or cross_training.

function.name: parse_run_file
function.description: Parse an uploaded .fit or .gpx file, log it in coach.db, and record it permanently in history.db (original file, all samples; failed and duplicate uploads are recorded too) (duplicates are detected, not re-inserted). Pure code -- ALWAYS use this rather than estimating a run's numbers. If data_quality_warning is set, tell the athlete what's missing.

athlete_notes.description: Anything the athlete said about the run.

function.name: match_run_to_program
function.description: Find the pending session (same day, else +/-1 day) this run corresponds to. If match is null, ask the athlete what the run was -- don't guess.

function.name: compare_run_to_program
function.description: Deterministic comparison of a logged run against its session (distance or, for time-based sessions, duration; HR cap; HR drift), marks the session done, and updates ALL pattern signals automatically. Relay the notes; a signal with action_threshold_met=false is 'watching', true means the pattern repeated and you should say what you're changing. Omit program_row_id for an unplanned run.

function.name: record_missed_session
function.description: Mark a pending session as missed (the athlete said so, or a week review found no file) and update the missed-session streak. Never add missed volume to another session.

function.name: write_program_revision
function.description: Every change to future sessions goes through this: supersede the affected rows and add replacement sessions (a move = supersede + add on the new date). Run with dry_run=true FIRST when the athlete asks to move something: it warns about hard sessions landing on adjacent days or doubled-up days, so you can raise that before agreeing. If you proceed against your advice, say so in summary and keep a guardrail (e.g. an HR cap).

items.description: A program row. Required: session_date (ISO), session_type. Distance OR duration.

week_num.description: Optional; inferred from the session it replaces.

function.name: schedule_checkin
function.description: Create an extra check-in bound to a session, a signal streak, or (last resort) a date. Plans already come with weekly, time-trial and end-of-block check-ins; use this for anything else (e.g. 'ask about the knee after Saturday's run').

function.name: get_due_checkins
function.description: List check-ins that should fire now (date reached, session passed, or streak reached). Run this on a daily schedule; for each, call check_trigger_staleness before acting.

function.name: check_trigger_staleness
function.description: Call FIRST for every due check-in. Marks it fired, or stale_cancelled if the session it depended on was replaced. If stale is true the plan changed since the check-in was written: tell the athlete, and answer from get_athlete_summary, not from the old prompt. If status is stale_cancelled, don't act on it at all.
